title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR 2 — Amyraut: Christ's justice said to enter
pass_a_gloss: GAR 2: It is no more absurd to say Adam's sin or singular act entered than to say Christ's righteousness entered. So Amyraut paraphrases this verse: through one man, Jesus Christ, true righteousness was introduced into the world—said of imputed righteousness no less than of inhering. If imputed righteousness may be said to be introduced or enter, why not imputed sin also?
pass_b_english: GAR. 2. It is not more absurd if it is said that sin, or Adam's singular action, entered, than if it is said that Christ's righteousness entered. But so speaks the distinguished Amyraut in a paraphrase of this verse: through one man who is Jesus Christ, true righteousness was introduced into the world, which is said of imputed righteousness no less than of inhering. To those whom it does not displease if imputed righteousness is said to be introduced or to enter, why should it not please, if imputed sin also is said to enter?
source_text: GAR. 2. Non est absurdius si dicatur peccatum, aut actio singularis Adae introiisse, quam si dicatur Christi justitia introisse. At ita loquitur Clar. Amyr. in paraphrasi huius versus, per unum hominem qui Iesus Christus est, vera justitia introducta est in mundum, quod de justitia imputata, non minus quam de inhaerente dicitur. Quibus non displicet si dicatur justitia imputata introduci vel intrare, quidni placeat, si dicatur etiam, peccatum imputatum introire?

choices.choice: If Christ's justice enters, so may imputed sin
